description:
kith-jmap/src/lib.rs: the Dispatcher has two separate registration methods — register() for owner-role handlers and register_peer() for peer-role handlers. The API forces every caller to know which map to use, and mis-registration (using register() for Peer/deliver, or register_peer() for Chat/get) silently returns unknownMethod at runtime for that method.

The only protection is a debug_assert! in dispatch_one() (line 490) that fires if a method appears in BOTH maps simultaneously — but it does not fire if a method is registered in the WRONG map.

The register() doc comment warns 'Do NOT use this for peer-role methods' but this is a social contract enforced only by prose documentation. The METHOD_ROLES table (line 264-292) already encodes which role each method requires, but register() ignores it entirely.

This is a defensive-code-forcing problem: every call site of register() and register_peer() must manually verify role assignment against METHOD_ROLES, duplicating the role table in every registration call.

Fix: eliminate the distinction between register() and register_peer(). Instead, accept a Box<dyn Any> and look up the required role from METHOD_ROLES at registration time, routing to the correct internal map automatically. Or: use a single trait with a role() method that the dispatcher can check. Either approach removes the per-call-site burden of knowing which map is correct.
title: kith-jmap: Dispatcher allows registering handler in wrong map with no compile-time check
